correctness.rationale: For K_{3,b}, b>=3, every simple cycle has four or six edges. A 5-edge shattered support would be five edges of a 6-cycle, but its 4-positive/1-negative trace would require two same-side edges, impossible; hence VC<=4. A depth-6 online tree has an all-positive path of six edges of a hexagon; after its first five edges the closing sixth edge is forced, contradicting the zero sibling. The boundary K3,3 has exactly 15 cycles, excluding depth/VC 4, and supports shatter 3. For K3,4, an explicit 4-edge support shatters all 16 traces and a complete 32-leaf depth-five certificate is supplied; embedding proves all b>=4. Independent enumeration found exactly 15 and 42 cycles, exact VC 3,4 and Ldim 3,5; inspected Git certificate has 31 internal nodes, 32 distinct consistent leaves, no repeated queries.

evidence: Circumference-based upper VC bound is <=5 in K3,b; reviewed claim gives sharp <=4 and adaptive Ldim exactly 5 for b>=4.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier general bound is weaker and says nothing sharp about online dimension; generic upper bounds cannot imply the new pair.
